problem.summary: The real release package still exposed stale user-facing version and update-note surfaces even though the public manifest had already been promoted to 0.2.5.
rootCauses: The WebUI top-left version is sourced from /api/version, which reads cli/VERSION; the source runtime still reported 0.2.4.
common/ecorex_release_notes.py still carried the v0.2.4 release notes payload.
The public download page kept 0.2.4 HTML fallback text and a 0.2.4 site.js cache-busting query.
The one-click installer scripts self-reported 0.2.4 even when the manifest version was 0.2.5.
The admin console fallback version still defaulted to older 0.2.2 display text.

changes: Updated cli/VERSION, desktop runtime cli/VERSION, and Python package metadata to 0.2.5.
Replaced root and staged-runtime release notes with v0.2.5 runtime/tool matrix update notes.
Updated the public site version fallback, updatedAt fallback, and site.js cache-busting query to 0.2.5.
Updated Windows and macOS one-click installer script self-reported version and Windows installer User-Agent to 0.2.5.
Updated admin console fallback version and admin API VERSION to 0.2.5.
Updated the deployment manifest notes to explicitly describe v0.2.5 display and update-note alignment.
Adjusted focused backend contract tests for the new release display version.

validation.staleDisplayScan: Only intentional v0.2.4 references remained in fix text and legacy schema tests; no critical display source matched stale 0.2.4 fallback strings.
